title: Injective sheaves have surjective restriction maps
statement: Let X be a ringed space [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism], U' ⊆ U open subspaces, and I an injective O_X-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category; def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Then the restriction map $I(U)\to I(U')$ is surjective. Consequently, for open U,V ⊆ X and any injective I, the map $I(U) \oplus I(V)\to I(U\cap V)$, $(a,b)\mapsto a|_{U\cap V} - b|_{U\cap V}$, is surjective.

proof.text: For each open V, take P_V = O_X[h_V], the free presheaf module on the representable h_V. Since the category of opens is a poset, its sections over T are free on a singleton if T is contained in V and free on the empty set otherwise. This is the extension-by-zero presheaf in the source proof. Set A_V = P_V^# using [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Composing the sheafification adjunction with [lem-weil-pbc-free-yoneda-presheaf-module] gives an equivalence Hom(A_V,I) with I(V). Naturality in V follows by the left naturality equations for the sheafification and free-module adjunctions, followed by yonedaEquiv_naturality; this explicitly identifies precomposition with A_{V\prime} to A_V with restriction.

For V\prime contained in V, the inclusion induces P_{V\prime} to P_V. Its section map is Finsupp.mapDomain on the map Hom(T,V\prime) to Hom(T,V). This indexing map is injective because its source is a subsingleton. Finsupp.mapDomain_injective and PresheafOfModules.mono_of_injective therefore give a monomorphism of presheaves. Module sheafification preserves finite limits [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-sheafification-exact]; hence it preserves this monomorphism, giving Mono(A_{V\prime} to A_V) by typeclass inference. No stalk computations are needed.

Given s in I(V\prime), use the inverse Hom-section equivalence to obtain A_{V\prime} to I. Apply Injective.factors [def-sp-injective-resolutions] along the monomorphism A_{V\prime} to A_V to obtain f:A_V to I. The naturality identity of step 1 and the factorization equation show that the section corresponding to f restricts to s. This proves restriction surjectivity for all inclusions of opens.

For open $U,V\subseteq X$, apply Step 3 to the inclusions $U\cap V\subseteq U$ and $U\cap V\subseteq V$. Given $c\in\mathcal I(U\cap V)$, choose $a\in\mathcal I(U)$ restricting to $c$ and take $b=0\in\mathcal I(V)$. Then $(a,b)$ maps to $a|_{U\cap V}-b|_{U\cap V}=c$, proving that $\mathcal I(U)\oplus\mathcal I(V)\to\mathcal I(U\cap V)$ is surjective.

split_report.summary: Split the Stacks 01EA argument into four proof steps. Extension by zero of the structure sheaf is built inline as the module sheafification of the explicit presheaf, which represents sections; stalks of a sheafification and stalkwise exactness make the nested-open map a monomorphism; injectivity gives surjectivity on sections, and the two-open difference-map consequence is elementary. No new nodes were needed.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the 09MR Mayer–Vietoris paragraph's assertion that sections of an injective sheaf restrict surjectively to an intersection, together with the resulting difference-map surjectivity.

tool_uses.why: Its generic ringed-space clause (5) is the stalkwise exactness criterion needed to turn the explicit injective stalk maps of the extension-by-zero morphism into a monomorphism; the unit has no replacement for this general sheaf fact.

lean.statement: theorem injective_restriction_surjective (X : RingedSpace.{u}) {U' U : Opens X} (hU : U' ≤ U) (I : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X)) [Injective I] : Function.Surjective (fun s : I.val.obj (Opposite.op U) => (I.val.map (homOfLE hU).op).hom s) ∧ ∀ (V W : Opens X), Function.Surjective (fun p : I.val.obj (Opposite.op V) × I.val.obj (Opposite.op W) => (show I.val.obj (Opposite.op (V ⊓ W)) from (I.val.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left : V ⊓ W ≤ V)).op).hom p.1) - (show I.val.obj (Opposite.op (V ⊓ W)) from (I.val.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right : V ⊓ W ≤ W)).op).hom p.2))
